AbstractText.Label: AIMS AND OBJECTIVES
AbstractText.content: To examine evidence-using a range of outcomes-for the effectiveness of school-based mental health and emotional well-being programmes.

AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: It is estimated that 20% of young people experience mental health difficulties every year. Schools have been identified as an appropriate setting for providing mental health and emotional well-being promotion prompting the need to determine whether current school-based programmes are effective in improving the mental health and emotional well-being of young people.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: A systematic search was conducted using the health and education databases, which identified 29 studies that measured the effectiveness of school-based universal interventions. Prisma guidelines were used during the literature review process.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Thematic analysis generated three key themes: (i) help seeking and coping; (ii) social and emotional well-being; and (iii) psycho-educational effectiveness.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: It is concluded that whilst these studies show promising results, there is a need for further robust evaluative studies to guide future practice.

AbstractText.Label: RELEVANCE TO CLINICAL PRACTICE
AbstractText.content: All available opportunities should be taken to provide mental health promotion interventions to young people in the school environment, with a requirement for educational professionals to be provided the necessary skills and knowledge to ensure that the school setting continues to be a beneficial environment for conducting mental health promotion.
